Title: Diagnosis of test `testMath280`

Details:
The test `testMath280` creates a `NormalDistribution` object with mean 0 and standard deviation 1, then it calls the `inverseCumulativeProbability` method on a probability value of `0.9772498680518209`.

The flow of the `inverseCumulativeProbability` method starts in `NormalDistributionImpl.inverseCumulativeProbability(double)` which has special cases for `p == 0` and `p == 1`. For other values, it delegates to the superclass method `AbstractContinuousDistribution.inverseCumulativeProbability(double)`.

Within this method, the input probability is first validated to ensure it lies within [0, 1]. Then a root-finding function is created representing the difference between the cumulative probability function and the target probability `p`.

The root-finding process requires bracketing an interval containing the root. This interval is obtained by calling three methods implemented in `NormalDistributionImpl`:
- `getDomainLowerBound(double p)` returns -MAX_VALUE if p < 0.5 or the distribution mean otherwise.
- `getDomainUpperBound(double p)` returns the mean if p < 0.5 or MAX_VALUE otherwise.
- `getInitialDomain(double p)` provides an initial guess near the mean ± 1 standard deviation depending on p relative to 0.5.

Then the solver attempts to bracket the root, and finally finds the root using the solver.

The `cumulativeProbability(double x)` method calculates the CDF using the error function erf for the normal distribution.

Since the failing test uses p=0.9772498680518209, which is > 0.5, the domain lower bound is set to the mean (0.0), the upper bound is set to Double.MAX_VALUE, and the initial guess is mean + std deviation (0 + 1 = 1.0).

The likelihood of failure here arises if the bracketing or root finding does not converge or throws an exception because the root is not bracketed correctly or the solver fails.

The test code does not catch or assert any expected exceptions, so a MathException thrown during root finding or cumulative probability computation likely causes the failure.

Next steps would be to verify if the bracketing and solver utilities are robust enough and confirm the handling of edge cases in the cumulativeProbability and inverseCumulativeProbability methods.

Hence, the fault likely occurs in the bracketing or solving process during inverseCumulativeProbability in the superclass or possibly due to cumulativeProbability throwing exceptions deep in error function evaluation.

Classes/methods to consider fixing:

org.apache.commons.math.distribution.NormalDistributionImpl.inverseCumulativeProbability(double)
org.apache.commons.math.distribution.AbstractContinuousDistribution.inverseCumulativeProbability(double)
org.apache.commons.math.distribution.NormalDistributionImpl.getDomainLowerBound(double)
org.apache.commons.math.distribution.NormalDistributionImpl.getDomainUpperBound(double)
org.apache.commons.math.distribution.NormalDistributionImpl.getInitialDomain(double)

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
